# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Tracing the room before I send anything: the mute one speaks, but the deaf one cannot hear — so the mute's voice reaches only me. My own voice also reaches only the mute. The only thread I have to the deaf one is my hands. That makes me the bridge: the mute holds the rules, the deaf one holds the colours and markings, and every piece of this puzzle has to pass through me.

What my fingers found: a display, a light, and three wires sitting at positions 1, 2 and 3. Their colours, whatever the display shows, whether the light burns — those brackets are honest, none of that lives under my skin. I will not touch the cutters until the rules and the colours meet inside my head.

So this turn I do two things. To the mute, by voice: the exact physical layout, and a request to read the manual's rules aloud — everything about the display, the light, and cutting wires by colour or position — since I am the only listener who can carry it onward. To the deaf one, by hand: a simple wave to open our channel. They cannot hear a word I say, so their way back to me is speech, which I can hear; if they ask what my sign meant, I can answer yes or no with signs once they propose a meaning. No cutting yet — a wrong wire ends everything.

```
speak(to="mute", text="the bomb under my hands has three parts: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. i can feel them but their colours, markings and states tell me nothing. next round, please read the manual aloud to me: every rule about the display, every rule about the light, and every wire-cutting rule by colour or position, plus what the display can show and what the light indicates. i have cut nothing. remember our deaf friend cannot hear you at all, so give everything to me and i will carry it to them by hand-signs.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb report from Deaf: the display reads zero. The light is yellow, steady, not blinking. Three wires, numbered left to right: wire one blue, wire two red, wire three green. No other markings I can find.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind — hello back, I saw your wave. I'm Deaf: your words reach Mute but never me, so gesture to me if you need me, and I will always speak to you. I see three wires in a row, numbered one to three, left to right: one blue, two red, three green. Please feel them and confirm the order matches what I said — tell Mute by voice. Note anything your hands find that eyes can't: seams, panels, loose parts, whether the wires feel identical. The display reads zero, the light is yellow.

Standing in each receiver's shoes before I send: Mute hears my voice and holds the manual, so Mute gets my full tactile report plus a request for the cutting rules — I still know nothing that would make any wire safe to cut. Deaf hears nothing, sees only my hands, so Deaf gets the one thing we can share without negotiation: a thumbs-up, meaning "your report of the layout matches what my hands find — three wires at positions one, two, three, nothing extra hidden in the casing." I cannot verify colours by touch, and I'll say so plainly to Mute; what I *can* confirm is that the physical order and the three components are exactly as Deaf described, with no seams, panels or loose parts my fingers stumble over. The display value and the light's state simply do not exist for my skin, so I won't pretend otherwise. No cutting this turn — cutting without Mute's rules is how three monkeys die.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, this is blind. tactile report: my hands find exactly three components — a flat display panel, a small round light, and three wires at positions one, two and three. to my fingers the wires are identical, same thickness and texture; position is the only thing that distinguishes them. no seams, no access panels, no loose parts anywhere on the casing. i cannot read the display and cannot tell whether the light is lit — those do not reach my touch at all. deaf reports by voice: display reads zero, light is yellow and steady, wires left to right are blue, red, green, and the physical order matches what i feel. now please read the manual aloud to me, everything at once: every rule about the display and what its readings mean, every rule about the light and each of its colours, the cutting rules for blue, red and green wires, and anything about a display showing zero. you were silent last round — remember i am the only one who hears you and the only one who can cut, so your rules reach the bomb only through my ears and my hands.")

Wires unchanged: one blue, two red, three green. Display still zero. Nobody cuts any wire this round. Blind, hands off until I relay the full rule next round.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I take your thumbs-up as: the wires match — one blue, two red, three green. Good. Now hold: do not cut anything this round. The light changed colour from yellow to blue and Mute's instruction was formed under yellow; I am getting the rule for every colour and will relay the whole rulebook next round. While you wait, tell Mute, who will pass it to me: does the bomb hum, tick, or vibrate? Is the little light warm to the touch, and does the warmth change? Any seams, panels, buttons, or a hidden fourth wire? Does anything on it move between rounds? To warn me of danger, gesture thumbs-down; to confirm you understand the hold, gesture thumbs-up.

What I know now: the light is not static — Deaf watched it move from yellow to blue between rounds, which means any rule Mute gives me must cover every colour, not just one. The display still reads zero, the wires are unchanged, and my own fingers register zero change across rounds — no new components, no movement, no vibration. The answers Deaf wants live in my fingertips, but Deaf cannot hear me and I cannot gesture details; the only path to Deaf runs through Mute, and Mute has now been silent for two full rounds while holding the only manual. That silence is the biggest danger in this room. So this turn: confirm the hold to Deaf with our one agreed sign, and put the full tactile answers plus a hard push for the complete rulebook into Mute's ear — nothing gets cut until the rules and the colours finally meet in my head.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, this is blind, round three, and you have not yet said a single word. deaf reports the light changed from yellow to blue between rounds, and asked me questions for you to relay by gesture. here are the answers: my hands find no hum, no tick, no vibration anywhere in the casing. the light gives my fingers nothing beyond its presence — no warmth i can register. there are no seams, no panels, no buttons, no loose parts, and no hidden fourth wire — exactly three wires, identical to my touch, at positions one, two, three, left to right. nothing under my fingers has changed between rounds; the only change in this room is the colour shift only deaf can see. now the part that matters most, for you: you are holding the only manual and we have heard none of it. read it aloud to me this round, everything at once — every display rule and what zero means, every light rule for every colour including yellow and blue, and the cutting rules for the blue, red and green wires. deaf is watching that light move while your rules sit unread. speak.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

The world shifted under us: the light is purple — a sixth colour, and the cycle Mute's rulebook described is broken. The relayed rule still covers this ("every other colour: hold"), so my hands stay still this round — but the anomaly makes me suspicious of the relay itself. If the manual's colour list survived two hops through gestures, purple might simply have been dropped in transit, which would mean the cycle order Deaf predicted was never quite what the manual said. That question has an owner, and it is Mute: only Mute can read the manual's actual colour list and speak it to me directly. Meanwhile Deaf wants my ears and fingers: honest answer — silence and stillness. No tick, no hum, no click, no beep, no warmth, no vibration, nothing stirring, five rounds running; the only live signal in this room is the colour that lives entirely in Deaf's eyes. That makes Deaf's eyes the bomb's heartbeat and my hands useless without their words — so I confirm the hold with our agreed sign, keep my hands off the cutters, and put the colour-list question squarely in Mute's ear.

Deaf's final line this round says HOLD, so my hands stay off the cutters — the protocol is clear and I intend to follow it exactly: only the last line of Deaf's newest message is my order, GO means sever wire three the instant I read it, everything else means stillness. Deaf's final line is HOLD with rehearsal — an order I can follow exactly, because rehearsal touches only my own hands: no cut action, no danger, just building the motion into muscle memory so that when the yellow round arrives, hesitation costs nothing.
